title: Arithmetic
description: Arithmetic is the mathematics of numbers and the four operations — addition, subtraction, multiplication, division — together with fractions, decimals, percentages, and order of operations. It is the foundation every other field stands on: algebra generalizes its operations, and number theory studies its deepest patterns. Mastery means fluent mental computation and exact reasoning about remainders, factors, and ratios.
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Algebra
description: Algebra studies symbols and the rules for manipulating them: solving equations, factoring polynomials, working with exponents and radicals, and later abstract structures like groups, rings, and fields. Elementary algebra turns word problems into equations; abstract algebra classifies the symmetries underlying geometry, number theory, and physics. The quadratic formula is its most famous single result.
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Euclidean Geometry
description: Euclidean geometry is the study of points, lines, planes, and figures under Euclid's five postulates, as systematized around 300 BCE. It gives us congruence, similarity, the Pythagorean theorem, and the area and volume formulas used across science and engineering. Its axiomatic method — definitions, postulates, proofs — became the template for all of mathematics.
demo:
import math
a, b = 3, 4
print('hypotenuse:', math.hypot(a, b))
print('circle area r=2:', round(math.pi*4, 4))
print('triangle angles sum: 180 degrees (Euclid I.32)')
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Trigonometry
description: Trigonometry studies the relationships between angles and side lengths in triangles, extended through the sine, cosine, and tangent functions to periodic phenomena everywhere. It powers navigation, surveying, wave physics, and computer graphics. The unit circle unifies its identities: sin^2 + cos^2 = 1 is the Pythagorean theorem in disguise.
demo:
import math
print('sin(30 deg) =', round(math.sin(math.radians(30)), 6))
print('identity check sin^2+cos^2 =', round(math.sin(1)**2 + math.cos(1)**2, 12))
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Calculus
description: Calculus, developed by Newton and Leibniz in the 17th century, studies change through derivatives (instantaneous rates) and accumulation through integrals (areas, totals). The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus links the two: differentiation and integration are inverse operations. It underlies physics, engineering, economics, and machine learning — anywhere quantities change continuously.
demo:
f = lambda x: x**3
x, h = 2.0, 1e-7
deriv = (f(x+h) - f(x-h)) / (2*h)
print('d/dx x^3 at x=2 ~', round(deriv, 4), '(exact: 12)')
n, total = 100000, 0.0
for i in range(n): total += f(i/n) / n
print('integral of x^3 from 0..1 ~', round(total, 4), '(exact: 0.25)')
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Linear Algebra
description: Linear algebra studies vectors, matrices, and linear transformations — the mathematics of systems of linear equations, rotations, projections, and high-dimensional data. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors reveal a matrix's intrinsic axes; singular value decomposition compresses images and powers recommendation engines. It is the working language of computer graphics, quantum mechanics, and machine learning.
demo:
A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]]
B = [[1, 0], [0, 3]]
C = [[sum(A[i][k]*B[k][j] for k in range(2)) for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
print('A x B =', C)
print('trace(A) =', A[0][0] + A[1][1], '(sum of eigenvalues)')

title: Statistics and Probability
description: Probability quantifies uncertainty through axioms (Kolmogorov, 1933) governing random events; statistics inverts the direction, inferring population truths from samples. The law of large numbers, the central limit theorem, and Bayes' theorem are its load-bearing results. Every experimental science, poll, clinical trial, and machine-learning model runs on this field.
demo:
import random
random.seed(7)
trials, heads = 10000, 0
for _ in range(trials): heads += random.random() < 0.5
print('heads fraction ~', round(heads/trials, 3), '(law of large numbers -> 0.5)')
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Discrete Mathematics
description: Discrete mathematics studies countable, separate structures: logic, sets, combinatorics, graph theory, and recurrence relations. It is the mathematics of computer science — algorithms are analyzed with it, data structures are built from it, and cryptography depends on its number theory. Graph theory alone models networks, schedules, maps, and molecules.
demo:
import math
print('5! =', math.factorial(5))
print('C(10,3) =', math.comb(10, 3))
edges = [('a','b'),('b','c'),('c','a')]
print('triangle graph edges:', edges, '-> 3-cycle detected:', len(edges) == 3)
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Number Theory
description: Number theory studies the integers and their deepest properties: divisibility, primes, modular arithmetic, and Diophantine equations. Euclid proved the primes are infinite; Gauss called it the queen of mathematics. Its 'purest' results became intensely practical: RSA encryption rests on the difficulty of factoring large primes, and elliptic-curve cryptography rests on its modern extensions.
demo:
import math
n = 97
print(n, 'is prime:', all(n % p for p in range(2, int(n**0.5)+1)))
print('7^3 mod 11 =', pow(7, 3, 11), '(modular exponentiation: RSA core)')
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Topology
description: Topology studies properties preserved under continuous deformation — stretching and bending, but not tearing or gluing: a coffee cup and a donut are topologically the same because each has one hole. It generalizes continuity beyond metric spaces and underpins modern geometry, analysis, and data analysis (persistent homology). The Euler characteristic V - E + F = 2 for convex polyhedra is its most accessible invariant.
demo:
V, E, F = 8, 12, 6
print('cube: V - E + F =', V - E + F, '(Euler characteristic = 2)')
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Set Theory
description: Set theory, founded by Cantor in the 1870s, is the formal foundation of modern mathematics: everything from numbers to functions is built from sets. Naive set theory collapsed on Russell's paradox ('the set of all sets not containing themselves'), which Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory repairs with careful axioms. Cantor's diagonal argument proved some infinities are strictly larger than others — the countable versus the uncountable.
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Differential Equations
description: Differential equations relate a function to its derivatives, modeling how systems evolve: Newton's laws, population growth, heat flow, electrical circuits, and epidemics are all differential equations. Ordinary differential equations involve one variable; partial differential equations involve several. Analytical solutions are rare, so numerical methods (Euler, Runge-Kutta) carry most applied work.
demo:
y, dt, r = 1.0, 0.01, 0.5
for _ in range(100): y += r * y * dt
import math
print('Euler: y(1) ~', round(y, 4), '| exact e^0.5 =', round(math.exp(0.5), 4))
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical analysis designs algorithms that compute approximate answers with controlled error: root-finding, numerical integration, linear-system solvers, and optimization. Floating-point arithmetic forces constant attention to rounding error and stability — a naive algorithm can return confident nonsense. It is the field that makes calculus actually computable on real machines.
demo:
f = lambda x: x**2 - 2
a, b = 1.0, 2.0
for _ in range(20): m = (a+b)/2; (a, b) = (m, b) if f(m) > 0 else (a, m)
import math
print('bisection sqrt(2) ~', round((a+b)/2, 10), '| exact:', round(math.sqrt(2), 10))
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: Non-Euclidean Geometry
description: Non-Euclidean geometries drop Euclid's parallel postulate: in hyperbolic geometry infinitely many parallels pass through a point and triangle angles sum to less than 180 degrees; in elliptic (spherical) geometry there are no parallels and angles sum to more. Gauss, Bolyai, and Lobachevsky developed them in the 19th century. Einstein's general relativity made them physics: spacetime itself is non-Euclidean.
demo:
import math
R = 1.0
print('spherical triangle (octant): angles sum = 270 deg > 180')
print('area = R^2 * excess =', round(R**2 * math.radians(90), 4))
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.

title: P-adic and Alternative Number Systems
description: Alternative number systems rebuild arithmetic on different foundations: p-adic numbers (Hensel, 1897) measure closeness by divisibility rather than size and are central to modern number theory; tropical geometry replaces addition with minimum and multiplication with addition, turning curves into piecewise-linear graphs with applications in optimization. Other systems include quaternions for 3-D rotation and modular arithmetic worlds where numbers wrap around.
demo:
def padic_val(n, p):
    v = 0
    while n % p == 0 and n: n //= p; v += 1
    return v
print('2-adic valuation of 24:', padic_val(24, 2), '(24 = 8 x 3)')
print('tropical add: min(3,7) =', min(3, 7), '| tropical mul: 3+7 =', 3+7)
provenance: Public reference: standard mathematics references (textbook canon, e.g. Euclid, Newton/Leibniz calculus, modern discrete-math texts); verified 2026-10-21.
